title: Why Do I Crave Salt? Causes, When to Worry and the Blood Tests That Check
summary: Why do I crave salt? See how sweat, fluid loss, PMS, low iron and Addison disease explain it, when to get urgent care, and which blood tests check.
body_markdown:
Table of contents


**Most salt cravings follow salt and fluid loss** , from heavy sweating, vomiting, diarrhea or water pills, the everyday ways the body runs short of sodium \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]\[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html) \]\[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]. **A salt craving that lasts, with tiredness, weight loss, dizziness on standing or darker skin, can be a sign of adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease)** , where the adrenal glands make too little cortisol and usually too little aldosterone \[[4](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/symptoms-causes) \]\[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \].


No vitamin deficiency is a recognized cause of craving salt. Low iron is linked to a different craving, an urge to chew ice \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]\[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001538.htm) \]. The blood tests that check the medical causes are a morning cortisol test with ACTH, a sodium and potassium check (part of a basic or comprehensive metabolic panel), a ferritin test for iron, and glucose or HbA1c when the craving comes with heavy thirst \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \]\[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]\[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \]\[[11](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/symptoms-causes) \].


## When salt cravings need urgent care


**Go to the emergency room or call 911 for signs of an adrenal crisis** , a sudden, severe worsening of adrenal insufficiency that can be the first time the condition shows itself \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]\[[12](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000357.htm) \]. Its signs include \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]\[[12](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000357.htm) \]:


- severe nausea, vomiting or diarrhea;
- belly pain or flank pain (pain in the side, between the ribs and the hip);
- confusion, fainting or loss of consciousness;
- dizziness or lightheadedness, with low blood pressure;
- severe weakness, a rapid heart rate or fast breathing;
- high fever, or signs of dehydration.


An adrenal crisis can be fatal without treatment, and it is treated with hydrocortisone given by injection right away \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]\[[12](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000357.htm) \]. People already diagnosed with adrenal insufficiency use their emergency injection first, then go to the hospital \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \].


**Also call 911 for dehydration or heat illness with danger signs** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]\[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000056.htm) \]:


- loss of consciousness, or any change in alertness such as confusion or a seizure;
- a fever over 102°F (38.8°C);
- a rapid pulse or rapid breathing with heat illness;
- symptoms that do not improve, or get worse, despite fluids.


**Low blood sodium can also become a life-threatening emergency** , and a drop over less than 48 hours is more dangerous than a slow one \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]. Its symptoms include confusion, restlessness, seizures, headache, nausea and vomiting \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \].


None of these should wait for a blood test. The tests in this article are for a craving that lasts or keeps coming back, never for sudden symptoms.


## Reading the pattern: what comes with the craving


**What comes with the craving narrows the cause before any test.** Salt cravings on their own are common and not a diagnosis. These are the patterns the sources describe:


Pattern Likely cause What checks it


After heavy sweating, a hot day or hard exercise, with thirst or muscle cramps Salt and fluid lost in sweat \[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html) \]\[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000056.htm) \] Usually nothing beyond fluids. A sodium test if it keeps happening \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]\[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/sodium-blood-test/) \]


After vomiting, diarrhea, or starting a water pill (diuretic) Salt and fluid loss \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]\[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \] Sodium and potassium on a basic or comprehensive metabolic panel \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]\[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]


Lasting, with tiredness, weight loss, poor appetite, dizziness on standing or darker skin Adrenal insufficiency, most often Addison disease \[[4](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/symptoms-causes) \]\[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \] Morning cortisol and ACTH, with sodium and potassium. An ACTH stimulation test confirms \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \]


Craving salt and also chewing ice or wanting to eat non-food things Low iron, which is linked to the ice craving (pica) \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]\[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001538.htm) \] Ferritin and a complete blood count (CBC) \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]\[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \]


With heavy thirst, needing to urinate often, or unplanned weight loss Uncontrolled diabetes, which causes heavy urination \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]\[[11](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/symptoms-causes) \] Glucose and HbA1c \[[11](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/symptoms-causes) \]\[[16](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]


In the days before a period, with bloating and other cravings, month after month Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) \[[17](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/premenstrual-syndrome) \]\[[18](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001505.htm) \] The timing itself, over at least three cycles in a row \[[17](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/premenstrual-syndrome) \]


Since childhood or the teen years, with muscle cramps or spasms, weakness, dizziness or tingling A rare inherited salt-wasting kidney condition, such as Gitelman syndrome \[[19](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/gitelman-syndrome/) \] Electrolyte tests, since the condition unbalances potassium, magnesium and calcium \[[19](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/gitelman-syndrome/) \]


## Sweat, dehydration and fluid loss


**Sweating removes salt as well as water.** The CDC’s workplace heat guidance explains that heavy sweating during strenuous activity depletes the body’s salt and moisture, and that low salt levels in the muscles cause painful heat cramps \[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html) \]. Thirst, very heavy sweating and muscle cramps are early signs of heat illness \[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000056.htm) \].


**Dehydration happens whenever you lose more fluid than you take in** \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]. Besides sweating, the common causes are fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and urinating a lot, which uncontrolled diabetes and water pills (diuretics) can cause \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]. The signs of mild to moderate dehydration are \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]:


- thirst and a dry or sticky mouth;
- urinating less, with darker yellow urine;
- headache;
- muscle cramps;
- dry, cool skin.


For heat cramps, the CDC advises water plus a snack or a drink that replaces carbohydrates and electrolytes, and avoiding salt tablets \[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html) \]. MedlinePlus likewise suggests sipping a sports drink or a lightly salted drink, and not taking salt tablets \[[13](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000056.htm) \]. Get medical help for heat cramps that do not ease within an hour, or right away if you have heart problems or follow a low-sodium diet \[[2](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html) \].


**Sweating, vomiting, diarrhea and water pills can also lower blood sodium** (hyponatremia) \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]. Its symptoms are confusion, irritability, fatigue, headache, loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting, and muscle weakness, spasms or cramps \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]. A[sodium](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/sodium) blood test confirms it, and it is part of both the basic metabolic panel (BMP) and the comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]\[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/sodium-blood-test/) \]. A sodium result is usually read alongside the other electrolytes, such as[potassium](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/potassium) \[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/sodium-blood-test/) \]. For the full list of signs, see[symptoms of low sodium](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-low-sodium) and[electrolyte imbalance symptoms](https://mitohealth.com/guide/electrolyte-imbalance-symptoms) .


For cravings tied to training or a low-carb diet, see[cravings after exercise](https://mitohealth.com/symptoms/cravings-after-exercise) and[cravings on keto](https://mitohealth.com/symptoms/cravings-on-keto-diet) .


## Adrenal insufficiency and Addison disease


**Craving salty foods is a listed symptom of adrenal insufficiency** , a condition in which the adrenal glands do not make enough cortisol \[[4](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/symptoms-causes) \]\[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]. The Endocrine Society lists salt craving specifically for primary adrenal insufficiency, also called Addison disease \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]. In Addison disease the adrenal glands themselves are damaged, most often by an autoimmune process, so they usually make too little aldosterone as well as too little cortisol \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]\[[20](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28723023/) \]. Aldosterone is the adrenal hormone that helps regulate blood pressure \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \].


In secondary adrenal insufficiency, the problem is in the pituitary gland, which does not send enough ACTH (adrenocorticotropic hormone) to tell the adrenal glands to make cortisol \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]. Aldosterone production is normal in this type \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \], and salt craving is not among its listed features \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]. Taking certain steroid medicines, such as prednisone, hydrocortisone or dexamethasone, is one of the causes of secondary adrenal insufficiency, sometimes a temporary one \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \].


**The most common symptoms come on slowly and are easy to miss** \[[4](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/symptoms-causes) \]\[[20](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28723023/) \]:


- long-lasting tiredness;
- muscle weakness;
- loss of appetite and weight loss;
- belly pain.


Other symptoms include nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, low blood pressure that drops further when you stand up and causes dizziness or fainting, joint pain, irritability or depression, low blood sugar, and irregular or missed periods \[[4](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/symptoms-causes) \]\[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]. Addison disease can also darken the skin, especially on scars, skin folds, the lips and the inside of the cheek \[[4](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/symptoms-causes) \]\[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \].


Because these symptoms are vague, Addison disease is often diagnosed late, sometimes only once an adrenal crisis happens \[[20](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28723023/) \]. For more on the condition and its symptoms, see[low cortisol symptoms and causes](https://mitohealth.com/blog/low-cortisol-symptoms-and-causes) ,[symptoms of low cortisol levels](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-low-cortisol-levels) and[adrenal dysfunction and insufficiency](https://mitohealth.com/blog/adrenal-dysfunction-and-insufficiency) .


### The tests for adrenal insufficiency


**A morning cortisol and ACTH test is the Endocrine Society’s initial screen when its gold-standard test cannot be done first** \[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \]. Cortisol is normally at its highest in the morning, which is why the sample is taken early in the day \[[21](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cortisol-test/) \]. ACTH also varies through the day, so it is drawn early in the morning too \[[22](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003695.htm) \].


Result What it suggests


Low morning[cortisol](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/cortisol) with high ACTH The adrenal glands themselves are not responding, as in Addison disease \[[22](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003695.htm) \]\[[21](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cortisol-test/) \]


Low morning cortisol with low ACTH The pituitary is not signaling enough, or steroid medicines are suppressing ACTH \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]\[[22](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003695.htm) \]


Low sodium with high potassium A pattern seen in Addison disease, together with low cortisol \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[20](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28723023/) \]


**An ACTH stimulation test confirms the diagnosis.** It measures cortisol in blood taken before and after an injection of ACTH, and it is the test used most often to diagnose adrenal insufficiency \[[23](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/adrenal-insufficiency-addisons-disease/diagnosis) \]. The Endocrine Society guideline calls it the gold standard \[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \]. A blood test for antibodies against 21-hydroxylase then looks for the autoimmune cause \[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \].

## Low iron and the urge to chew ice


**Low iron is linked to a craving for ice, not salt.** As iron deficiency anemia worsens, one listed symptom is a desire to eat ice or other non-food things \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]. Eating non-food items is called pica, and a lack of certain nutrients, such as iron and zinc, may trigger these unusual cravings \[[8](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001538.htm) \].


So if you crave salt and also find yourself chewing ice, the ice craving is the part that points to iron. Heavy, long or frequent periods are a common cause of iron loss \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \], and pregnancy and heavy menstrual bleeding raise the risk of low iron \[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \]. Other symptoms of low iron include tiredness, weakness, dizziness and shortness of breath \[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \].


**A[ferritin](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/ferritin) test shows your iron stores, and a complete blood count (CBC) shows whether anemia is present** \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]\[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \]. A low ferritin may mean iron deficiency anemia or another condition related to low iron \[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \]. For what the number means, see[ferritin levels](https://mitohealth.com/guide/ferritin-level) and[symptoms of low ferritin](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-low-ferritin) . Mito offers a[ferritin blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/ferritin) and a[CBC](https://mitohealth.com/products/complete-blood-count-cbc-with-differential-and-platelet-count) .


## Salt cravings before a period


**Food cravings are a listed physical symptom of PMS** , together with thirst and appetite changes, bloating and weight gain \[[17](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/premenstrual-syndrome) \]\[[18](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001505.htm) \]. ACOG and MedlinePlus describe food cravings in general rather than salt cravings specifically, and both list limiting salt and sugar among the self-care steps for PMS \[[17](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/premenstrual-syndrome) \]\[[18](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001505.htm) \].


PMS symptoms follow a pattern: they appear in the days before a period, month after month \[[17](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/premenstrual-syndrome) \]. To count as PMS, symptoms must be present in the 5 days before a period for at least three cycles in a row \[[17](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/premenstrual-syndrome) \]. A craving that continues through the whole month does not fit PMS. For other patterns in women, see[cravings in women](https://mitohealth.com/symptoms/cravings-in-women) .


## Heavy thirst and high blood sugar


**Craving salt together with heavy thirst and frequent urination points to fluid loss through the urine.** Feeling very thirsty and urinating more often are classic symptoms of diabetes \[[11](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/symptoms-causes) \], and uncontrolled diabetes is a listed cause of dehydration \[[1](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000982.htm) \]. Other diabetes symptoms include feeling very hungry even after eating, blurred vision, fatigue and sores that do not heal, and type 1 diabetes can also cause unexplained weight loss \[[11](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/symptoms-causes) \].


A[glucose](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/glucose) test, also part of the CMP, measures your blood sugar when the sample is taken, and[HbA1c](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/hba1c) shows your average over the past two to three months \[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]\[[16](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]. For HbA1c \[[16](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]:


- below 5.7% is normal;
- 5.7% to 6.4% is prediabetes;
- 6.5% or higher is diabetes.


For more on thirst as the main symptom, see[why am I always thirsty](https://mitohealth.com/blog/excessive-thirst) . ## Rare kidney salt-wasting conditions


**A few rare inherited kidney conditions make the kidneys lose too much salt into the urine.** Gitelman syndrome is one: its common features include salt craving, painful muscle spasms, muscle weakness or cramping, dizziness, and tingling of the skin, most often on the face \[[19](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/gitelman-syndrome/) \]. Its signs usually appear in late childhood or adolescence, and it upsets the balance of potassium, magnesium and calcium in the body \[[19](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/gitelman-syndrome/) \]. A salt craving since childhood with these symptoms is a reason to see a clinician.


## Stress and everyday cravings


**The sources reviewed for this article do not list everyday stress as a medical cause of salt craving.** The Endocrine Society states that the adrenal glands do not get “adrenal fatigue” or lose function because of mental or physical stress, and that true adrenal insufficiency is rare and diagnosed with standard tests \[[6](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/adrenal-insufficiency) \]. If a salt craving lasts and comes with tiredness, weight loss or dizziness on standing, a morning cortisol test is the way to check, whatever your stress level.


## Which blood tests check salt cravings


**The basic check is a metabolic panel plus a morning cortisol test.** A comprehensive metabolic panel measures sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate and glucose, along with kidney and liver markers, in one blood draw \[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]. A basic metabolic panel covers sodium, potassium, chloride, carbon dioxide, glucose and kidney markers \[[24](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/basic-metabolic-panel-bmp/) \]. Each result points in a different direction:


Result What it suggests


Low sodium Salt loss from sweating, vomiting, diarrhea or water pills, or Addison disease, among other causes \[[3](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000394.htm) \]\[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/sodium-blood-test/) \]


High sodium Dehydration, often from not drinking enough, diarrhea or water pills \[[14](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/sodium-blood-test/) \]


Low sodium with high potassium and low cortisol The pattern of Addison disease. A clinician confirms with an ACTH stimulation test \[[5](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000378.htm) \]\[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \]


Low ferritin Low iron stores, which fits an ice craving more than a salt craving \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]\[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \]


High glucose, or HbA1c of 6.5% or higher Diabetes, which causes thirst and fluid loss through the urine \[[11](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/symptoms-causes) \]\[[16](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/) \]


All normal The common blood causes are less likely, which fits a craving that follows sweating or comes before a period


### Mito tests for salt cravings


- **[Morning cortisol test](https://mitohealth.com/products/cortisol-am) .** The first check for adrenal insufficiency, the condition in which salt craving is a listed symptom that a blood test can help find.
- **[Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)](https://mitohealth.com/products/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp)** or **[Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP)](https://mitohealth.com/products/basic-metabolic-panel-bmp) .** Sodium, potassium and glucose in one blood draw, for fluid and salt loss and the Addison disease pattern \[[15](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/comprehensive-metabolic-panel-cmp/) \]\[[24](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/basic-metabolic-panel-bmp/) \].
- **[ACTH blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/adrenocorticotropic-hormone-acth) .** Drawn with morning cortisol to tell an adrenal cause from a pituitary cause \[[9](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26760044/) \]\[[22](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/003695.htm) \].
- **[Ferritin blood test](https://mitohealth.com/products/ferritin) .** Iron stores, when the craving comes with chewing ice, heavy periods or tiredness \[[7](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000584.htm) \]\[[10](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ferritin-blood-test/) \].


None of these tests replaces a clinician’s assessment. A low cortisol result, or a sodium and potassium pattern that fits Addison disease, needs confirmation and treatment from a clinician.

## Frequently asked questions


### What vitamin deficiency causes you to crave salt?


No vitamin deficiency is a recognized cause of salt craving. Heavy sweating removes salt along with water, and craving salt is a listed symptom of adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease), where the adrenal glands make too little cortisol and usually too little aldosterone. Rare inherited kidney conditions that leak salt into the urine, such as Gitelman syndrome, also list it. Low iron is linked to a different craving: an urge to chew ice or eat non-food things, called pica. A ferritin test checks iron stores, and a morning cortisol test with sodium and potassium checks the adrenal pattern.


### Is craving salt a sign of dehydration?


It can go with it. Heavy sweating, vomiting, diarrhea and water pills all remove both water and sodium from the body. Thirst, a dry mouth, dark urine, headache and muscle cramps are the listed signs of mild to moderate dehydration. Call 911 for confusion, fainting, a seizure, or a fever over 102 degrees Fahrenheit with dehydration or heat illness. A sodium test, part of a basic or comprehensive metabolic panel, shows whether blood sodium is out of range.


### When should I worry about salt cravings?


Get emergency care right away for salt craving with severe vomiting or diarrhea, severe belly or flank pain, confusion, fainting or very low blood pressure, which can be signs of an adrenal crisis. See a provider soon if the craving lasts for weeks and comes with lasting tiredness, muscle weakness, poor appetite, weight loss, dizziness when you stand up, or skin that is darkening, since those are listed symptoms of adrenal insufficiency. Craving salt after a sweaty workout or before a period, without other symptoms, is common and usually passes.


### Why do I crave salt before my period?


Food cravings, thirst and appetite changes are listed physical symptoms of premenstrual syndrome, along with bloating. Neither ACOG nor MedlinePlus names salt specifically, and both list limiting salt and sugar among the self-care steps for PMS. Cravings that come only in the days before a period, month after month, fit PMS. Heavy periods can also lower iron, which is linked to a craving for ice rather than salt.


### Can stress make you crave salt?


The sources reviewed here do not list everyday stress as a medical cause of salt craving. The Endocrine Society states that the adrenal glands do not develop so-called adrenal fatigue from mental or physical stress, and that true adrenal insufficiency is a rare condition diagnosed with standard blood tests. A salt craving that lasts and comes with tiredness, weight loss and dizziness on standing is worth a morning cortisol test whatever your stress level.
